chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Sonny Greer, Ellington's colorful drummer
summary: Greer was a colorful, expressive painter of feelings rather than a swing drummer and never needed a drum book.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yes. Now, going back to drummers that I worked with, too, I think Sonny Greer was the most colorful. Sonny Greer wasn't a swing drummer, actually, but colorful. He could paint pictures. He could create feelings.
He was very expressive, very expressive. He knew exactly what to do with Duke's arrangements.
And he didn't have to read. It's just that there was never a drum book in that band.
